story.headline: SpaceX Is Funding an AI Bet Before the Proof

question: SpaceX after the IPO: exit liquidity, or the next ten-bagger?

call.line: SpaceX’s AI build is credible. The stock has already paid for 10 gigawatts it has not built.
actions: Value the AI arm on deployed gigawatts (0.4 today), not on the roughly 10 GW site plan.
Treat Starlink’s $4.4 billion of operating income as the collateral, not the upside.
Strip related-party and Anthropic-linked revenue out before calling AI demand proven.
flips: Deployed capacity climbs toward the site plan, quarter after quarter.
AI revenue arrives net of related-party deals and Anthropic keeps paying without the capital cycle doing the work.

against.name: Trey Henninger
against.claim: SpaceX at roughly 100 times trailing revenue would never qualify as a value investment, yet it is feasibly a ten-bagger: an extreme bull scenario could carry the company toward an 18 trillion dollar valuation or beyond over ten to twenty-five years.

settles.event: Quarterly deployed gigawatts will test the roughly 10 GW site plan against 0.4 GW operating now.
Anthropic’s $1.25B monthly commitment expires; payment durability will test contracted AI demand.
Bond pricing will show whether lenders still trust Starlink to carry AI spending.
A third trillion-dollar cash-burning listing would test Kevin Gee’s market-capacity concern.
